All settings

Every key you may set in .sdlc/config.json, grouped by block, with its scaffolded default and what it does. The short list a new adopter needs is on Configuration; start there.

Most people only need

  • Nothing here: the scaffolded values are the safe ones, and Configuration covers the handful you will touch first.
  • Use this page to look a key up by name, or to see what a block does before you turn it on.
  • Anything marked opt-in is off until you turn it on. Turn on one at a time, then run /sigma-doctor.

How to read this page

  • Default is what the scaffold writes (from the template the setup command copies), not always what the code assumes when a key is absent. Where the two differ the row says so.
  • Opt-in means the feature is off until you set it to the JSON boolean true (or the value the row names). The text “true” or the number 1 leaves it off.
  • Keys that start with an underscore are notes written by the scaffold; they are not settings and are not listed.
  • A key marked “not in the scaffold” is read when present but is not written by init; an update never rewrites the file, so copy a new block in from the template in the installed plugin.
  • A value of the wrong type is usually read as the default, with a note. Check the result with /sigma-doctor.
  • Defaults that are provisional, or limits that have not been measured, are said so in the row.

discovery: where goals come from and in what order

Goal intake, ordering and the label names the loop reads and writes. Label meanings are on Labels.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
discovery.sourcelocal-goalsWhere goals live: local-goals (files in .sdlc/goals/) or github (issues labelled with the goal label; needs gh). Init chooses it.
discovery.orderprioritypriority sorts by the priority label, oldest first within a tier; created is strict oldest-first. A goal with no priority sorts last.
discovery.github.repoemptyThe owner/name of the repository whose issues are goals.
discovery.github.goal_labelsdlc:goalThe label that marks an issue as a goal.
discovery.github.in_progress_labelsdlc:in-progressOverlay written while a goal is claimed.
discovery.github.parked_labelsdlc:parkedLabel for a goal waiting on a person.
discovery.github.goal_blocked_labelsdlc:blockedCode-managed label for a goal that found a blocking dependency. Clears itself when the blocker closes.
discovery.github.blocked_labelemptyOptional label you set yourself to say “do not auto-pick” (a spend gate, a legal review). The loop never writes it. Empty changes nothing.
discovery.github.blocking_labelsdlc:blockingDerived label put on a blocker while any open issue still names it. Removed by itself.
discovery.github.needs_label_labelsdlc:needs-labelOverlay for a goal whose declared unit has no matching label yet. Clears when a person creates the label.
discovery.github.needs_unit_labelsdlc:needs-unitOverlay for a goal that declares no unit at all, used only with discovery.no_dangling_goal.
discovery.github.priority_label_prefixpriority:The prefix the priority labels use. Change it if your repository already has its own scheme, or every such issue ranks as unprioritised.
discovery.github.assigneenull (not yet decided)@me or a login: pick only issues assigned to that user, so several people can share a board. null is “not decided”; the setup command fills in @me the first time it adopts a GitHub repository. An empty string is a deliberate “no filter”.
discovery.reconcile.modeoffon runs one throttled sweep per batch that corrects one class only: a closed issue still carrying an in-progress or not-eligible label. Anything else goes to a proposal a person approves.
discovery.reconcile.ttl_minutes60Minutes between two surveys (a survey costs about 13 GitHub calls).
discovery.reconcile.open_issue_modeoffSeparate opt-in that lets decisive corrections on open issues apply on their own instead of waiting for approval.
discovery.dag.modeshadowThe stored dependency map: shadow compares it with the board mirror and never changes a pick; on holds goals from the map; off reads and writes nothing. Anything unrecognised reads as shadow.
discovery.dag.ttl_minutes60A map older than twice this is not used unless a change check ran in the last ten minutes.
discovery.dag.orderchainchain puts the goal that unblocks the most work first inside a priority tier; off does not. It never crosses a priority tier.
discovery.dag.cycle_commenttrueWhether a refresh posts one comment per distinct dependency cycle.
chain.max_members100Largest closure the chain planner will plan from the stored map; a larger one is refused with its count, never truncated. See the note below on where this key lives.
gh_quota.rest_reserve_percent10Percentage of GitHub’s reported REST limit kept in reserve. Below it, the auto-unpark sweep and the reconcile sweep defer. Provisional default. See the note below on where this key lives.
discovery.dependency_gate.modeonBefore a goal is claimed, a goal whose declared prerequisite is still open is left untouched and the pick moves on. off turns it off.
discovery.auto_unpark.modeonEach pick re-checks blocked goals; when every recorded blocker has closed, the block is lifted and the goal returns to the queue. A parked goal is never resumed this way. off opts out.
discovery.auto_unpark.interval_minutes10The sweep runs at most once per this many minutes. Provisional.
discovery.blocking_priority_overridetrueA goal that is also labelled as blocking sorts ahead of others in its own priority tier, never above a higher tier.
discovery.blocker_promotion.modealwaysA blocker’s priority is raised to match what it blocks; nothing is ever lowered. off disables it.
discovery.no_dangling_goal.enabledoff (opt-in)Sets aside a goal that declares no unit (it gains the needs-unit label and resumes once a unit is declared). Needs the .sdlc/features/ folder as well.
discovery.no_dangling_goal.coreemptyName of a registered unit. When set, an undeclared goal is classified into units by an AI judgment instead of being set aside.
label_drain.default_priorityP2Priority label given to an armed issue that has none; an existing priority is kept.
label_drain.arm_pulled_blockerstrueWhen arming a run label, also arm open blockers outside the label.
label_drain.kinds{}Maps exact run-label names to kinds. Otherwise a label’s kind is its name up to the first : or /.
Where two keys live

The scaffold writes chain.max_members and gh_quota.rest_reserve_percent inside the discovery block, but the code that reads them looks for them at the top level of the file (checked by search in the code). The configuration reference also names them at the top level. If you need to change either, put it at the top level.

discovery.github.project: the board mirror

Mirrors each goal’s state onto a GitHub Projects board. It needs the project scope on gh and is fail-open: if the board cannot be written, the loop still runs on issues and labels. The behaviour is on The project board.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
discovery.github.project.enabledtrue in the template; init keeps it off until the board offer is answeredTurns the board mirror on. With no board pinned or reachable nothing is written.
discovery.github.project.numbernullPin your board’s number if one already exists. Without a pin Sigma looks up the title and, finding none, may create a board.
discovery.github.project.owneremptyThe organisation or user that owns the board. @me means the token’s own login.
discovery.github.project.titleemptyLook the board up by exact title when no number is pinned.
discovery.github.project.status_fieldStatusName of the status column.
discovery.github.project.priority_fieldPriorityName of the P0 to P4 column. false writes nothing.
discovery.github.project.queue_sourcestatusstatus: the Ready column is the pick queue. label: the goal label alone decides.
discovery.github.project.archive_donetrue in the scaffoldArchive a card once its goal completes. Only the boolean true archives; an absent key archives nothing.
discovery.github.project.columns.*Backlog, Ready, In Progress, QC, Done, Blocked, ParkedThe seven lane names (backlog, ready, in_progress, qc, done, blocked, parked). Rename one to match your board.
discovery.github.project.custom_fields{}Maps a custom single-select field name to an option name; stamped on issues Sigma itself files. A field or option the board lacks is skipped.
discovery.github.project.phase_fieldPhaseName of the Phase column; false disables Phase. Not in the scaffold; read when present.
discovery.github.project.mirror_priorityofftrue makes the pinned board’s Priority column Sigma’s. Not in the scaffold; read when present.
discovery.github.project.backfill_cap20Open goals carded per watcher tick (0 turns it off). Provisional. Not in the scaffold.
discovery.github.project.backfill_min_graphql1000The back-fill skips a tick when fewer GraphQL calls than this remain. Provisional. Not in the scaffold.

verify, tests and context: proof of done

The command that proves a goal works, and the settings around what counts as proof. Configuration has the short version.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
verify.commandemptyThe command that proves a goal’s change works.
verify.enforcefalse; on once a command is confirmedOn: record done and a merge are refused without fresh passing evidence from this run.
verify.timeout_minutes60 (not in the scaffold)Budget for one verify run; read when present.
verify.known_flakesabsentA person-approved, time-limited list of tests allowed to fail a full verify. Nothing adds an entry automatically. Each entry has a test id, a tracking issue, an approver, a record link, an expiry date and the bases it covers.
tests.runners{}Names a non-default test runner a plan’s test list may use: a command template with {file} and {name} placeholders, optionally with a pattern that marks a red run.
review.test_reviewfalseIndependent test review can block an approval: each acceptance criterion needs a real test.
context.documents[]Extra repository-relative documents added to the reviewer’s brief. Leave the key out for the built-in set.
context.inline_max_bytes16384A document larger than this is given to the reviewer as a pointer, not inlined.
quality.metricsabsentOptional list of metric commands compared at the merge-base and the head. Nothing runs while it is absent.
setup_wizard.dismissed[]Setup checks the repository has deliberately declined. Not in the scaffold.

work: worktrees, pull requests and merging

One worktree, branch and pull request per goal. The risky switches ship off. Configuration has the short version.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
work.enabledtrueOne worktree, branch and pull request per goal. Off means the loop edits the checkout directly.
work.baseemptyThe integration branch to cut from and target. Empty means the branch the loop started on. A goal that declares a unit is cut from the unit’s branch instead.
work.integration_baseemptyName a unit branch that is also your integration branch, so branch upkeep accepts it.
work.remoteoriginThe remote to push to.
work.branch_prefixsdlc/Prefix of a goal’s branch.
work.worktree_dir.sdlc/workWhere goal worktrees are cut.
work.auto_mergeoffoff never merges. protected merges only where the base branch requires checks or reviews. always merges any clean and safe pull request but still stops where protection could not be read.
work.protection_unreadableholdallow lets an always merge proceed when every unreadable protection source was refused with a permission error (a private repository on a free plan). Anything else reads as hold.
work.merge_methodsquashHow a merge lands, as written by the scaffold.
work.require_reviewchangeschanges parks on a request-changes review or unresolved thread; approval also needs an approval; off relies on branch protection.
work.max_review_cycles3Review-to-fix rounds before the goal is parked.
work.ci_requiredtruefalse stops waiting on checks the base branch does not require.
work.merge_pending_wait_s450Seconds one merge waits, re-reading every 45, on a check that has attached but not answered. Under 45 is raised to 45; over 7200 is capped.
work.merge_bypassoff (not in the scaffold)ruleset lets a merge land through the account’s ruleset bypass when a set of read-only conditions hold; anything unreadable parks.
work.checkpoint_prefixempty (not in the scaffold)Where a pre-pull-request checkpoint is pushed. Empty means the goal branch itself; wip/ pushes to wip/<N>.
work.rebase_upkeeponOn every pick of a goal that declares a unit, the unit branch is rebased onto the base. off turns that off. See Units of work.
work.unit_completionsurfaceWhat happens when a unit has no open issues left. surface prints a line and leaves a ledger note; off does nothing; draft-pr also opens the landing pull request as a draft.
work.reclaim_merged_worktreesfalseLets a bounded sweep remove the checkout of a goal worktree whose pull request has positively merged.
work.allow_secret_paths[]File names allowed through the commit-time check for secret-shaped names.
work.allow_secret_content[]Content patterns allowed through the commit-time check for credential-shaped lines.
session_release.grace_minutes15A dead session’s claimed-but-never-started goals are released once its entry has been quiet this long.
session_release.hold_minutes30A pick also releases a goal a live session has held this long with no work. 0 turns it off.
session_start.enabledoff (opt-in)Injects a short policy brief and an install check at the start of every session. Advisory only.

budget, handoff and followups: limits

A budget enforces only when set to a positive number. Each belongs to the session that started it, so several sessions can together spend several times one ceiling.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
budget.max_iterations20Goals per session.
budget.max_minutes480Wall-clock minutes from the session’s own start.
budget.max_tokens100000000Priced Claude-equivalent tokens, counted from phases with a full price.
budget.max_codex_raw_tokens0 (off)Measured Codex input plus output tokens. A phase-boundary admission stop, not a quota or a bill.
handoff.enabledtrueThe orchestrating session stops claiming and hands off to a fresh one.
handoff.after_goals20Hand off after this many goals.
handoff.after_context_tokensnull (derived)Hand off once the session’s own measured context reaches this. When null it is derived from the context at the first pick and the host window; provisional. 0 turns either trigger off.
followups.modein-goalA follow-up in the goal’s own feature joins that goal as a slice. file (exactly that string) opts back out to one goal per follow-up.
followups.max_added_slices10Cap on slices added to one goal; a whole number of at least 1, otherwise 10, never unlimited.
ai_filed.triage.enabledtrueTriage of issues the AI files: a deny-list can only park, then a bucket sets the priority. false restores plain queueing.
ai_filed.buckets.urgent / routine / unclearP2 / P3 / P4Priority given to each bucket. Each must rank below the human default priority, or every filing parks.
ai_filed.max_per_goal5AI-filed issues armed per goal.
ai_filed.max_per_run20AI-filed issues armed per run.
ai_filed.max_depth3Deepest chain of AI-filed issues filed from AI-filed issues.
ai_filed.cap_bypass_priorityP1Priority at or above which the caps do not apply.
ai_filed.on_capparkpark waits for a person; defer lets the auto-unpark sweep re-arm it, highest priority first, once the counter has room.
ai_filed.counter_pathstate/ai_filed_counter.jsonWhere the filing counter is kept.
ai_filed.counter_retention_days14Days of counter history kept.
ai_filed.migration.*10000; 30; 60; 3max_issues, max_writes_per_minute, rate_limit_pause_s, rate_limit_max_pauses: bounds for the one-off label migration.

gates, review and design: what must be true before a step

The gates are checks that refuse a step rather than advise. Configuration has the short version.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
gates.phase_record.enabledtruerecord done and a merge are refused unless every phase is on record, including an approved plan-review.
gates.plan_review.enabledoff (opt-in)Also refuses the pull-request push without an approving plan-review for the exact plan.
gates.hard_plan_gate.enabledoff (opt-in)Refuses the pull-request push for a goal with no plan, and on Claude Code the edit itself.
gates.hard_plan_gate.plan_freshness_hours24How recent a plan must be.
gates.stop_gate.enabledoff (opt-in)Refuses to let the agent stop with unplanned source changes in the working tree.
gates.stop_gate.plan_freshness_hours24How recent a plan must be.
gates.quality_ratchet.enabledoff (opt-in)A merge is refused when a required quality metric got worse beyond its tolerance.
gates.sealed_acceptance.enabledoff (opt-in)An author-blind breaker writes the goal’s acceptance tests, which are sealed red on the base.
gates.irreversible_actionsdeploy, delete, overwrite, spend, migrateAction classes the loop parks on rather than takes.
gates.on_blockparkWhat the loop does when a gate blocks.
decision_tieroffauto classifies a judgment-call park into an escalation tier and shows it; advisory only.
review.independenttrueAsks for a fresh, author-blind reviewer. An instruction to the agent; no code proves the maker did not influence the reviewer.
review.hostautoWhich mechanism gives this host an independent reviewer: auto, claude, cursor, codex, command or inline.
review.commandemptyA command that reads the review brief on stdin and prints a review; used with command. It is your command, trusted like verify.command.
review.timeout_seconds900Time limit for a review or sealed-test process.
goal_readiness.modewarnwarn prints missing sections and proceeds; require parks the goal; off checks nothing.
goal_decompose.enabledoff (opt-in)Flags an oversized goal before any tokens are spent.
goal_decompose.modeloglog annotates, park parks, file also files one meta-issue before parking.
goal_decompose.max_children8Cap on children one decomposition may file.
goal_design.enabledoff (opt-in)Retrofit gate: a goal without the designed label is parked and a design ticket filed before work.
goal_design.modefullMode of the design pass; scaffolded as full.
backlog_check.enabledoff (opt-in)Parks a picked goal that duplicates, is obsoleted by, or is blocked by other backlog items, before any tokens are spent.
backlog_check.actionparkpark parks a confident hit; flag only annotates.
backlog_check.similaritytfidftfidf or bm25.
backlog_check.dup_threshold / obsolete_threshold / park_threshold0.72 / 0.72 / 0.8Similarity scores for a duplicate, an obsolete hit and a park.
backlog_check.top_k8Candidates compared.
backlog_check.closed_window_daysautoHow far back closed work is compared.
backlog_check.embed.enabled / command / weightfalse / empty / 0.5Optional embedding command blended into the similarity.
backlog_check.mirror.ttl_minutes / closed_limit60 / 200Cache age and closed-issue read limit of the board mirror.
spend_approval.enabledoff (opt-in)Per-goal, single-use exemption from the park-on-expensive-action rule. Needs a marker as the first line of the issue body, written by an approver.
spend_approval.approvers[]Logins allowed to authorise. An empty or malformed list means nobody can.
spend_approval.classesspendAction classes the exemption can cover.
design.zonesabsentOwner-declared legacy and modern change zones, by glob.
design.restructure_lines40 (absent)Changed-line threshold above which a legacy file reads as a restructure.
architecture.system_rootdocs/architectureWhere the architecture document lives.

Model selection and companions

Model tiers are chosen per goal, not per session. See /sigma-model for the command.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
model_selectionauto in the scaffold (off in code if absent)auto predicts a tier per goal and runs its phases at it; off uses the session model.
model_selection_reviewer_floorsonnetReviewer phases never run below this tier. An unknown value reads as sonnet.
model_selection_max_tieropusPrice ceiling on the tier the router may resolve; the default keeps goal text from reaching the most expensive tier.
model_selection_signal_excludes[]Keyword signals the router should ignore on this repository.
model_host_overrides{}Host-specific substitutions for the tier resolver, limited to this plugin release’s approved Codex identifiers. A malformed mapping refuses before dispatch.

parallel: concurrent work

Two separate controls. The first is about one goal’s slices, the second about several goals. The difference is explained on Parallel and scheduled runs.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
parallel.enabledoff (opt-in)Run one goal’s independent slices concurrently, in waves, from a slice manifest.
parallel.max_concurrent3Widest wave of slices.
parallel.goals.enabledoff (opt-in)Return several backlog goals at once, one worktree and pull request each. Needs work.enabled.
parallel.goals.max_concurrent3Most goals at once. Size it to memory, not to the number of open issues.

resource: the resource guard

Every key is scaffolded as null, which means derived from this machine. A bad value reads as derived with a note. The fractions are policy ratios, not fitted to a real exhaustion: two recorded runs (macOS, and Linux in a 2 GiB container) fixed none of them.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
resource.modederived: enforceobserve logs the hold it would make and admits; off skips the check. The environment variable SIGMA_RESOURCE_MODE overrides it.
resource.reserve_fraction0.20 of memoryMemory kept free for the machine.
resource.max_share_fraction0.60 of memoryMost memory all sessions together may lease.
resource.cpu_reserve_coresone eighth of cores, at least 1Cores kept free.
resource.load_hold_ratio1.0 per coreOne-minute load per core above which load is reported high.
resource.swapout_hold_mb_per_sshown, never holdsWhen set, a swap-out rate above it holds.
resource.shedverifyWhat is stopped first under pressure: verify or off.
resource.shed_after3Consecutive critical samples (two seconds apart) before the shed stops the verify group.
resource.max_goalsno extra capHard cap on concurrent goals.
resource.max_verify_workersno extra capHard cap on concurrent verify workers.
resource.verify_cold_mbone eighth of memory per workerMegabytes one verify worker is assumed to need before any run has been measured. Unmeasured on any real machine.
resource.hold_alert_minutesno alertMinutes a hold may last before it is reported.

The team ledger and the background watchers that ride on it. As a team explains when to turn it on.

ledger.watch.log_max_bytes1048576Cap on the watcher log.
ledger.lease.ttl_hours12A claim by a crashed session expires after this. 0 never expires. Advisory.

ledger.autowatch.target_issue_onlytrueNever an open-ended pick.

Local records: action log and journal

Both are local to your machine and never published.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
action_log.enabledtrueThe local trace of loop activity that /sigma-log reads. Keep on. If the key is absent the code treats it as off.
journal.enabledoff (opt-in)A local activity journal: phase timings, gate verdicts and counts, never code or prose.

upkeep: keeping unit branches current

All of it ships off. Turning it on needs three things together; they are listed on Units of work. An unknown key, a wrong type or a contradictory pair in this block closes the whole block, and the doctor names the key.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
upkeep.enabledfalseProject opt-in; only the JSON boolean true opens it.
upkeep.window_hours12Hours since the last completed sweep before the next may start (1 to 8760).
upkeep.retry_minutes60Hold-off after an attempt that did not complete; never closes the window.
upkeep.units.include / exclude["*"] / []Case-folded globs for units the sweep may pick; exclude always wins.
upkeep.verify.timeout_minutes60With a 15-minute margin, the sweep’s total time cap.
upkeep.verify.clean_rebasefalseRead and checked; not acted on.
upkeep.backup.keep_days / keep_last14 / 5Prune removes backups older than keep_days but always keeps the newest keep_last of each unit.
upkeep.backup.former_prefixes[]Backup namespaces an earlier product wrote, pruned the same way.
upkeep.conflicts.resolveoffoff parks a conflict; mechanical resolves changelog-only conflicts; agent runs a capped resolver plus a reviewer. With no spend key set the agent level has no spend limit.
upkeep.conflicts.mechanical_without_verifyfalseLets the mechanical level run with no verify command.
upkeep.conflicts.union_paths[]Files whose two-sided pure additions the mechanical level unions.
upkeep.conflicts.agent.modelsonnetModel for the resolver.
upkeep.conflicts.agent.max_budget_usd_per_unit / spend_ceiling_usd_per_daynull / nullSpend caps for the agent level. Set at least the first.
upkeep.conflicts.agent.timeout_minutes / max_units_per_sweep30 / 5Time per unit and units per sweep.
upkeep.conflicts.agent.reviewer.enabled / modeltrue / sonnetThe independent reviewer of a resolution.
upkeep.conflicts.agent.credential_var / loginnull / scrubbedWhich credential the resolver uses; host runs on the watcher’s own login.
upkeep.triggers.*, upkeep.auto.*see the branching contractStill read and checked for one release; they no longer schedule anything.

Every part is off by default and opens only on the JSON boolean true (the text “true” or the number 1 stay off). A wrong-typed value reads as its default unless it is an enabled flag, which closes the block.

Other keys

KeyDefaultWhat it does
mode.defaultgoalWritten by init. Leave as scaffolded.

Environment variables

VariableWhat it does
SIGMA_RESOURCE_MODEoff, observe or enforce; overrides resource.mode everywhere.
SIGMA_UPKEEP_JOBExactly 1 on one machine opts that machine in to the branch-upkeep sweep. See Units of work.
SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_SOCKET_TOKENSlack tokens. Secrets stay in the environment, never in the file.
SIGMA_SMTP_PASSThe default name of the variable holding the email password for the agent watch.
SIGMA_TRUSTED_VERIFY_SHA256An operator’s approval of the verify command for one repository in a cloud environment. Only the operator sets it.
SIGMA_LEDGER_ALLOW_UNSERIALISEDLets ledger publishing proceed unserialised where the publish lock cannot be made; unset means refuse.
SIGMA_CODEX_BIN, SIGMA_CODEX_CMDChoose the Codex binary, and the launch command, for a Codex supervisor. See Parallel and scheduled runs.
Technical detail

This page is written from the scaffold template and the configuration reference in the repository: configuration. The rulebook keys are described further in the decision rulebook guide, the dependency keys in the dependency map guide. What enforces each setting, and on which host, is in enforcement.
